title: HITL IDS - data decision tree (flow alerts, Tier 1 to Tier 2)
source: Rules read from the code at commit dc58a09. Counts measured on a routed copy of data/demo.db (5,000 flows). Ground truth from data/processed/demo_ground_truth.json - shown to the reader only; the product never sees it.

dataTypes.name: Raw flow record
dataTypes.holds: CICFlowMeter output for one network flow: addresses, ports, protocol, packets, bytes, duration, 88 features

dataTypes.name: Detection alert
dataTypes.holds: Signature matches, model class and probability, evidence class, detection score, is_critical (fixed after detection, migration 23); combined score and severity (moved by verdicts within guardrails). The queue score is not stored: routing priority + (combined - detection), clamped 0-100 (apps/api/operational_queue.py:43)

dataTypes.name: Alert group
dataTypes.holds: Flagged alerts from one source IP; first member is the representative

dataTypes.name: Operational alert + triage state
dataTypes.holds: One queue item per group or single flow: route, stage, priority, band, Tier 2 recommendation and reasons

dataTypes.name: Tier 1 work
dataTypes.holds: Claim owner, status (available, in_review, completed, escalated), who finished it

dataTypes.name: Analyst verdict + feedback
dataTypes.holds: Outcome and reason; the mapped score change, requested and actually applied

dataTypes.name: Tier 2 case
dataTypes.holds: Who or what created it, status open -> investigating -> resolved, conclusion, resolution

nodes.question: What do the detectors say?
nodes.rule: fuse(): a rule matched AND the model predicts a class a matching rule asserts -> corroborated; a rule matched, model disagrees -> signature_override; no rule, model predicts an attack -> ml_only; else none.
nodes.why: Two independent detectors that agree are stronger evidence than one. The class says what kind of proof the analyst has: a checkable rule, a model opinion, or nothing.
nodes.evidence: tests/test_fusion.py (invariants I1-I4); counts from the routed demo copy

nodes.question: Score and severity
nodes.rule: corroborated: min(100, max(sig, ml) x 100 + 5); ml_only/none: ml x 100. Critical (is_critical) when score >= 80. Severity band (Low >= 1, Medium >= 40, High >= 70, Critical >= 80) capped by the attack class: Brute Force/DoS Medium, Web Attack/DDoS High, Infiltration/Botnet Critical, Port Scan Low.
nodes.why: Confidence says how sure the model is; the class says how much the finding is worth. Without the cap, every attack class read Critical.
nodes.evidence: tests/test_ranking.py asserts is_critical = score >= 80; 0 mismatches on demo.db

nodes.question: Was the flow flagged?
nodes.rule: evidence_class != 'none' -> flagged (goes to grouping). 'none' -> never grouped; each flow becomes its own routine queue item below every flagged item.
nodes.why: D4: a missed attack must stay findable. Grouping by source would hide one attack among the same host's benign flows.
nodes.evidence: Approved demo story AL-03086 (path E) is reachable only through this branch; test_a_high_scoring_unflagged_item_still_ranks_below_every_group

nodes.question: Group by source IP
nodes.rule: Sort flagged alerts by time. The next alert from the same source IP within 30 minutes of the group's last alert joins the group; otherwise a new group starts. One group = one queue item.
nodes.why: One attack produces hundreds of near-identical alerts. The analyst reads one item per event, not per packet flow (alert fatigue).

nodes.question: E1: auto-escalate?
nodes.rule: Any member with score >= 80 AND (corroborated [E1-flow-rule] OR a linked Suricata alert of severity <= 2 [E1-suricata]) escalates the whole group to a Tier 2 case - unless 5 new groups already escalated in that minute (then candidate).
nodes.why: Clear, corroborated, severe events should not wait for a Tier 1 click. Two detectors must agree, so a single detector cannot open a case alone.
nodes.evidence: Real packets 2018-02-14: 287,591 E1 flows, precision 0.99986, recall 1.0 by per-flow labels (analysis/spike/SPIKE-RESULT.md). Demo: E1 = 200 alerts, 0 benign

nodes.question: Tier 2 candidate?
nodes.rule: E3: score >= 90 AND attack severity >= 7 (Infiltration 9.5, Botnet 9.0, Web Attack 8.0, DDoS 7.5), OR the detectors disagree on the class, OR an E1 branch that the Admin switched off. Candidate = Tier 1 review with reasons; never automatic.
nodes.why: E3 alone made 342 wrong escalations on the stress set (precision 0.4722), so a human must confirm. DoS (6.5) and Brute Force (5.0) are below 7: high score alone does not make them candidates.

nodes.question: Fail-safe
nodes.rule: If routing cannot be evaluated (an exception), the item goes to routine Tier 1 with the reason. Routing never closes, dismisses or lowers an alert.
nodes.why: A software fault must never hide an alert or open a case by mistake.
nodes.evidence: Not exercised on demo data (0 failures in 4,085 routes)

nodes.question: Tier 1 claim
nodes.rule: Opening a row claims it for the analyst (status in_review). A system-routed Tier 2 case cannot be claimed. Claim expires after 15 minutes idle; owner or admin (with reason) can release.
nodes.why: Two analysts must not work the same alert. A claim left by someone off shift must not block it.

nodes.question: Why Tier 2: escalate or keep?
nodes.rule: On a candidate, the analyst reads the reasons and chooses Escalate to Tier 2 (opens a case, records 'escalate' +15) or Keep in Tier 1 (closes the recommendation). A reason is required for both.
nodes.why: The machine recommends; a human decides and states why. The reason is part of the audit record.

nodes.question: Verdict
nodes.rule: Confirmed Malicious -> +10; Suspicious -> 0; Expected Activity -> -15; False Positive -> -30. The verdict completes the Tier 1 work.
nodes.why: A verdict teaches the system, so the next similar alert ranks better. The size of each step is fixed in configuration.

nodes.question: Guardrails
nodes.rule: The change is capped at -30 / +20. A negative change cannot push a Critical alert (score >= 80) below 70, nor an Infiltration alert below 75. The score stays within 0-100.
nodes.why: One person's verdict must not bury a severe alert or swing it without limit.
nodes.evidence: Path C: false positive on 99.89 requested -30, held at 70 (actual -29.89). Path D: +10 on 100 capped to 100.

nodes.question: Family learning gate
nodes.rule: Similar alerts (same family) move only after 3 agreeing verdicts at agreement >= 0.67. A group verdict counts once per family.
nodes.why: One wrong verdict must not re-rank a whole family.

nodes.question: Tier 2 case
nodes.rule: Start investigation (reason) -> record conclusion (finding + final class + reason) -> resolve (reason). Resolve stays off until a conclusion exists. A resolved case is read-only; a response plan is approved, never executed.
nodes.why: A case cannot close without a recorded finding; the closed record cannot change.

A.story: 80 FTP brute-force flows from one external source. Rule SIG-FTP-BRUTE-FORCE and the model agree, score 100, so E1 opens a Tier 2 case with no Tier 1 click. The expert starts, concludes and resolves it.

B.story: 57 flows from one internal host; only the model flags them (Infiltration), score 99.6. No rule, so no E1. E3 makes it a candidate (severity 9.5 >= 7). The analyst reads Why Tier 2 and escalates. Escalate +15 is capped at 100 (+0.4).

C.story: One web flow the model calls Web Attack (99.89). Ground truth: benign. E3 recommends Tier 2; the analyst keeps it in Tier 1 and marks False Positive. The critical floor holds it at 70, not 69.89: it stays visible.

D.story: 197 DoS flows from one source in 13 minutes, model only, score 100. DoS severity 6.5 < 7, so not a candidate: routine Tier 1. The analyst confirms; +10 is capped at 100.

E.story: One flow the model calls Benign (score 36.94, Low). Ground truth: an attempted Web Attack. It is not grouped and sits below all flagged items, but it is in the queue. The analyst finds it and confirms; +10 applied (36.94 -> 46.94, Medium).
